key_insight: AEAPTMS passivation makes perovskite surface electrostatics more uniform, boosting and stabilizing the light-induced surface photovoltage by suppressing grain-boundary barriers.
engineering_relevance: This suggests amino-silane molecular passivation can directly improve perovskite solar-cell stability and reduce photovoltage losses by engineering the nanoscale carrier landscape.
method: Amplitude-modulated Kelvin probe force microscopy (KPFM) to map dark CPD and illuminated SPV.
Compare untreated vs AEAPTMS-passivated mixed-cation, mixed-halide perovskite thin films.
Separate grain-boundary and grain-interior potential responses and test wavelength-dependent SPV.
evidence_signal: Passivation narrowed dark CPD spread from about 45.7 to 14.6 mV, increased steady-state SPV from about 345 to 417 mV, and reduced the stabilization time constant from about 840 to 470 s.
watch_item: These nanoscale surface-potential gains should be validated against full device durability and performance, since KPFM measures local film dynamics rather than complete solar-cell operation.
paper_title: Understanding surface potential dynamics of passivated perovskites via Kelvin Probe Force Microscopy
